llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions are internally consistent with its stated purpose (running ExtendScript in local Adobe apps), but it inherently executes arbitrary scripts with full filesystem access so use only with trusted code and review scripts before running.

dimensions.detail: Name and description claim cross-platform Adobe automation; the code writes a JSX file and invokes platform-native runners (cscript on Windows, osascript on macOS) to execute ExtendScript in the listed Adobe apps. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or external services are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and handler implement a runScript command that executes arbitrary ES3 (ExtendScript) in target Adobe apps. SKILL.md correctly states that ExtendScript has filesystem access; the runtime writes temp files and executes them. This is expected for the stated purpose but is high-risk by design — untrusted scripts can read/write/delete local files or perform other side effects.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with included handler.js and test_ps.js; no install spec or external downloads. There is no network fetch or archive extraction, so install risk is low.

llm.guidance: This skill legitimately provides a bridge to run ExtendScript inside local Adobe apps and the implementation matches that purpose. However, it will execute arbitrary JSX code on your machine and ExtendScript has full filesystem access (File/Folder), so only run scripts you trust. Before installing or enabling autonomous use: (1) ensure Adobe apps are installed and that you accept cscript (Windows) / osascript (macOS) being used; (2) audit any script text you pass to runScript for destructive or exfiltrating behavior; (3) test in a disposable environment or with non-sensitive files; (4) do not grant this skill to agents or integrations that may construct scripts from untrusted inputs. If you need safer operation, require the skill to only run vetted script templates rather than raw user-provided code.
